title: CPRA request — aggregate California surrogacy birth data and related data documentation

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CPRA request — aggregate California surrogacy birth data and related data documentation
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Government Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request the following records concerning live births occurring in California from January 1, 2015, through the most recent available records as of the date of this request.

This request seeks aggregate, de-identified statistical information and related data documentation. I am not requesting names, individual birth certificates, court orders, or other personally identifying information. Please include responsive information maintained in birth-registration, vital-statistics, and related registration or amendment processing systems.

**1. Annual surrogacy birth counts**

For each birth year and county of birth, the number of live-born children whose records identify a surrogacy or gestational-carrier arrangement, including parentage established by a judgment under Family Code § 7962.

Please use any maintained surrogacy indicators, registration or processing codes, or relevant notations. These include, where available, the AVSS “SURR” variable documented in the June 23, 2016 AVSS Variables/Definitions, “Surrogate Birth” comments described in CDPH’s January 2016 registration handbook, and equivalent fields in successor systems.

Include qualifying original registrations and amended or replacement records, counting each child once.

If surrogacy births cannot be separately identified, please provide, as a separately labeled fallback, annual counts by county of births registered or amended pursuant to a pre-birth or post-birth court order establishing parentage. Please distinguish available order or processing categories and identify the criteria used for each table.

**2. Parents’ countries of birth**

For the births identified under item 1, annual statewide counts by the recorded country of birth of each legal or intended parent listed on the birth certificate, with the parent fields reported separately.

Please identify the fields used and whether they describe the listed legal or intended parents, genetic parents, or gestational carrier. Include unknown or unrecorded categories where available. Keep any broader parentage-order fallback population separately labeled.

**3. Repeated parentage across births**

Annual aggregate counts of:

- Distinct individual parents listed on three or more qualifying children’s birth records within any rolling 12-month period;
- Distinct parent pairs meeting that threshold; and
- The total number of distinct qualifying children associated with those parents or parent pairs, reported separately for each measure.

Counts by calendar year are acceptable if rolling 12-month counts are not available through ordinary database extraction. Please identify the counting period and year-assignment method used.

Apply the threshold statewide, including births occurring in different California counties. Please provide statewide annual totals and county-of-birth breakdowns where available. If existing data permit, also provide the number of separate deliveries represented, so multiple children from one delivery can be distinguished from children born in separate deliveries.

If exact figures cannot be released, I am willing to accept counts of distinct individual parents and, separately, parent pairs grouped into bands of 3–5, 6–10, and 11 or more qualifying children within the applicable counting period. Statewide reporting, merging bands, and suppression of exact child totals within bands are acceptable where necessary to satisfy disclosure requirements.

If this item requires additional record linkage or custom analytical work, please advise me of the work and estimated cost before proceeding. Please continue processing the remaining items independently.

**4. Data definitions and coding documentation**

Please provide the relevant portions of existing data dictionaries, field definitions, code lists, and registration or amendment instructions describing:

- Surrogacy and gestational-carrier indicators, including AVSS “SURR,” “Surrogate Birth” comments, and equivalent successor-system fields;
- Parentage-order and amendment processing categories;
- Parent country-of-birth fields and whose information they represent; and
- Existing parent-linkage, deduplication, plurality, or delivery-identification methods relevant to the requested counts.

Please include applicable documentation for the requested period, including documented changes in field availability or meaning.

**Format, disclosure, and costs**

Please provide responsive electronic records under Government Code § 7922.570, preferably in CSV or Excel if available in a format CDPH holds or uses. Please identify the latest date covered and label partial-year or provisional data.

If small-cell restrictions prevent release at the requested detail, I am willing to accept suppressed tables, statewide totals, or combined-year totals. Please provide the applicable suppression policy and all reasonably segregable, nonexempt portions, citing the specific legal basis for any withholding.

Before incurring any charge, including compilation, extraction, or programming charges under Government Code § 7922.575, please provide an itemized estimate and obtain my written authorization.

If responsive information is maintained differently or requires clarification, please assist me in identifying available records and practical alternatives under Government Code § 7922.600. Please produce readily available records on a rolling basis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Whiteside

title: CBP records on Enhanced Border Security Partnership (EBSP) and International Biometric Information Sharing (IBIS)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. 552, I request copies of the following records held by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) about the Enhanced Border Security Partnership (EBSP) and the DHS International Biometric Information Sharing (IBIS) Program (DHS/ALL/PIA-095). Here, "IBIS" means the biometric information sharing program, not the former Interagency Border Inspection System, and I am not asking for records about any individual traveler. The date range for every item is 1 January 2022 to the date of search, unless an item says otherwise.

1. Agreements and requirement documents. EBSP agreements and arrangements, Enhanced Border Security Agreements (EBSAs), implementing arrangements, memoranda of understanding or cooperation, and Concept of Operations documents held by CBP that govern CBP queries to, or the receipt of responses from, a foreign partner under IBIS/EBSP. This includes any model or template texts, and the documents setting out the EBSP requirement for Visa Waiver Program (VWP) countries, including the DHS PowerPoint presentation "DHS Enhanced Border Security Partnership (EBSP) Requirement" (September 2022). It also includes the interconnection or technical arrangements for partner connections through the CBP Gateway or the Secure Real Time Platform (SRTP).

2. CBP procedures and training. Final CBP directives, policies, standard operating procedures, musters, job aids, user guides and training materials (including slide decks) on:
   a. starting biometric queries to foreign partners under IBIS/EBSP, including queries sent through the Automated Targeting System (ATS) to IDENT/HART;
   b. automated national identification number queries made from Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) applications, as described in DHS/ALL/PIA-095(b) and DHS/CBP/PIA-007(i);
   c. how responses from foreign partners are reviewed, marked, used, retained and shared onward in ATS, ESTA and TECS, including by officers at ports of entry and by the National Targeting Center, and how those responses are used in ESTA decisions; and
   d. how CBP carries out DHS Policy Statement 262-173.
   This item covers the component "procedures and operational policies" that DHS/ALL/PIA-095 (page 10) says each component must develop and finalize before it sends IBIS queries.

3. Partner status. Records showing which foreign partners are connected to CBP, or operational for CBP queries or responses, under IBIS/EBSP. For each partner, I would like the type of query (fingerprint or national identification number), the go-live or planned go-live date, and the current status. This item covers status lists, trackers and readiness or implementation reports.

4. Volume and results reports. Final periodic reports, dashboards or summaries received or produced by CBP that show the number of IBIS/EBSP queries and responses, match or hit rates, or results. This includes the monthly, quarterly and annual Office of Biometric Identity Management (OBIM) reports that DHS/ALL/PIA-095 says are "distributed to CBP, ICE, USCIS, and PLCY", and any CBP reports on ESTA outcomes linked to foreign-partner responses. Existing reports are enough; I am not asking CBP to create new records.

5. Privacy and oversight reviews. Final Privacy Threshold Analyses, privacy compliance reviews, audits, assessments and privacy-incident reports by or for CBP about IBIS/EBSP, ATS/ESTA use of foreign-partner data, or partner connections. This includes CBP's input to, and any findings from, the DHS Privacy Office Privacy Compliance Review that DHS/ALL/PIA-095 says will start "no later than three years or upon a substantive change to the program, whichever occurs sooner". It also includes CBP responses to any related DHS Office of Inspector General, Government Accountability Office or Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties review.

6. Deadline communications. From 1 January 2025 to the date of search: emails, memos and briefing papers exchanged between CBP and the DHS Office of Strategy, Policy, and Plans (including its Office of International Affairs), OBIM, or the Department of State about putting EBSP in place by, or meeting, the 31 December 2026 date for VWP countries to complete EBSP. This includes readiness assessments, connection schedules and compliance evaluations of particular countries.

Search suggestions: the Office of Field Operations (including the National Targeting Center and ESTA program staff), the Office of Information and Technology, the CBP Privacy and Diversity Office, and CBP's international affairs office. Suggested search terms: "EBSP", "Enhanced Border Security Partnership", "Enhanced Border Security Agreement", "EBSA", "International Biometric Information Sharing", "Secure Real Time Platform", "SRTP", and "national identification number" together with "ESTA".

Exclusions. These records are already public, so please do not search for them:
- DHS/ALL/PIA-095, 095(a) and 095(b), and the September 2024 Appendix update;
- the DHS/CBP/PIA-006 (ATS) and DHS/CBP/PIA-007 (ESTA) series, including PIA-006(e) and its December 2024 appendix update, and PIA-007(i) and 007(j);
- the DHS/OBIM/PIA-004 (HART) series;
- published System of Records Notices (including DHS/CBP-006, DHS/CBP-009 and DHS/CBP-011) and other Federal Register notices;
- DHS press releases, such as the 29 September 2025 release on the Bahrain EBSP; and
- the IBIS/EBSP information brochure (c. July 2022) published by Statewatch.
To avoid duplication, CBP may also leave out records it knows were released in full in DHS FOIA request 2023-HQFO-00480, if it lists them by title and date.

If any part of a record is withheld, please release all reasonably segregable portions, cite the exemption that applies to each withholding, and confirm that you considered the foreseeable harm standard. I am happy to receive records on a rolling basis, starting with items 1 and 2, and to discuss narrowing the scope if needed. I prefer electronic copies (PDF or native format).

I request a fee waiver under 6 CFR 5.11(k). I have no commercial interest in these records, and disclosing them is in the public interest. EBSP is a new condition for VWP participation, and it allows routine screening against foreign governments' biometric and identity databases. title: USCIS biometrics and background check procedures (CPMS, NaBISCOP, ASC SOPs, foreign partner queries)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: USCIS biometrics and background check procedures (CPMS, NaBISCOP, ASC SOPs, foreign partner queries)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. 552, I request copies of the following records:

1. User manuals, standard operating procedures, job aids, and training materials (including slide decks and course guides) for the Customer Profile Management System (CPMS), the CPMS Support Service (ESB2), and the National Appointment Scheduling System (NASS), created or in use from 1 January 2015 to the date of search.

2. The current "National Background, Identity, and Security Check Operating Procedures" (NaBISCOP), and every version or revision table issued after the version produced in Wagafe v. Biden, W.D. Wash. No. 2:17-cv-00094, Dkt. 665-22 (DEF-00431506), including any version issued in connection with the rescission of the Controlled Application Review and Resolution Program (CARRP).

3. The CARRP rescission notice or memorandum, and any replacement national security vetting policy, from 1 January 2026 to the date of search.

4. Standard operating procedures and guidance for biometrics collection at Application Support Centers (ASCs), including the ASC SOP(s) reviewed in the DHS Privacy Office's October 2017 CPMS/NASS Privacy Compliance Review and all later versions, and procedures for fingerprint waivers, biometric reuse, and identity verification.

5. Procedures, guidance, privacy threshold analyses, and agreements governing USCIS biometric or criminal history queries to foreign partner countries, from 1 January 2015 to the date of search, including:
   a. procedures for CPMS requests for background checks to a foreign partner country;
   b. USCIS use of the International Biometric Information Sharing program (DHS/ALL/PIA-095) – not the former Interagency Border Inspection System;
   c. the international arrangements cited in footnote 35 of the proposed rule "Collection and Use of Biometrics by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services" (90 FR 49062, 3 November 2025; docket USCIS-2025-0205);
   d. records on the "automated data-sharing capabilities" to query foreign partner countries for criminal history record information described in that proposed rule.

The following records are already public and are excluded: the c. 2021 NaBISCOP and the December 2010 NaBISCOP excerpt; the CARRP and FDNS training exhibits filed in Wagafe (Dkts. 665 and 666); the 2011 FDNS SOP; and published DHS/USCIS PIAs (including 008(a), 048(a), 057, 060 series, and DHS/ALL/PIA-095) and the 2017 CPMS/NASS Privacy Compliance Review.

I am happy to receive records on a rolling basis and in electronic format, and to discuss narrowing the scope if needed.

I request a fee waiver, as disclosure is in the public interest: it will contribute significantly to public understanding of how USCIS conducts biometric and background checks and shares biometric data with foreign governments, and I have no commercial interest. If a waiver is denied, I agree to pay fees up to $25; please contact me before exceeding that.

Thank you,
Jordan Ellis

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jordan Ellis

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Request for UCR master files for years not on the Crime Data Explorer
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records of the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program, CJIS Division:

The national master files for these collections, for every year the program holds before the first year the Crime Data Explorer (cde.ucr.cjis.gov) offers, as far back as the program's files go:
Return A (Offenses Known and Clearances by Arrest): every year before 1985
Supplement to Return A: every year before 1985
Age, Sex, and Race of Persons Arrested: every year before 1985
Arson: every year before 1985
Supplementary Homicide Reports: every year before 1985
Police Employee (LEOKA): every year before 1991 

For each year, the current version only; if identifying the current version would take more work than releasing every version the program holds, every version.
All documentation the program holds for those files: the record description (file layout) for each, and any other documentation, including coding manuals, code lists, records of changes to the files or their layouts, and notes that accompanied the files when they were distributed.
These are existing records: the program has distributed these master files to researchers before, on DVD.

Format. Electronic copies in the format the program keeps them, the fixed-width text master files, by download link or on a DVD or drive. No records need to be created or converted.

This request is for a noncommercial research project, not for commercial use. 

If any part of this request is denied, please release the rest, and cite the exemption for each part withheld.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Kaplan
